> **Spoilers.** The finished application, file by file — the state every
> chapter builds toward, and the tree every quote and transcript in this
> book was captured from. Use it to compare and to unstick; don't copy
> files wholesale. Generated code and artifacts (the `sqlc` output, the
> `moq` mocks, the `templ` output, the SBOM) are not reproduced here —
> `make generate` and `make sbom` produce them — and `go.sum` is what
> `go mod tidy` resolves. A few files are the app's own machinery rather
> than part of the build the chapters walk through — the workflow files
> under `.github/` and the `cmd/benchgate` tool — kept here so the tree
> is complete.

## `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

````yaml
name: ci

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          # The secrets scan is over the history; a shallow checkout would
          # scan one commit and pass vacuously.
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
          cache: true
      - name: check
        run: make check
      - name: race
        run: make race
      - name: build
        run: go build ./...

  bench:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          # The gate builds a test binary from the revision each baseline
          # names in its control-ref header, so the history has to be here.
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
          cache: true
      # The gate compares the working tree against a control revision built
      # and run in the same job, so the runner's hardware does not matter:
      # both sides ran there. It is the allocation budgets and the paired
      # time comparison that travel; the committed baseline files are the
      # record, not the comparison.
      - name: bench gate
        run: make bench-gate
````


## `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`

````yaml
# deploy.yml — the first CD step: a deploy that a human dispatches, gated by
# an environment, shipped over ssh. It takes effect once a remote and the
# production environment's secrets exist; until then the file documents the
# pipeline, and deploy/RUNBOOK.md's manual procedure is the same steps by
# hand.
#
# The shape, and why:
#
#   - workflow_dispatch, not push: a deploy is a decision, and the button is
#     the decision's record. The `ref` input defaults to main and can name a
#     tag for a rollback (the previous binary is what a rollback installs;
#     see the runbook).
#   - environment: production, where the repository's secrets live and where
#     required reviewers are configured. A workflow cannot name a secret the
#     environment does not grant it, so the environment is the gate, not the
#     YAML.
#   - `make check` before the build: the deployed artifact is built from a
#     tree the same gate passed, and the gate is the same one CI runs — a
#     dispatch on an old ref gets the same honesty machine as a push.
#   - CGO_ENABLED=0: the binary the release will ship is the binary the
#     deploy ships (chapter 49 makes that literal).
#   - The key is written to a file with mode 600 and the host key comes from
#     a secret, not ssh-keyscan: trust-on-first-use would accept whatever
#     answers the first connection, which is the one thing an ssh key is
#     supposed to prevent.
#   - The restart is followed by a readiness check through the app's own
#     /ready, over the loopback the unit binds: a deploy that shipped a
#     binary that cannot serve its database fails here, loudly.
#
# The four secrets: DEPLOY_HOST (the hostname), DEPLOY_USER (an account with
# sudo for the install and the restart), DEPLOY_SSH_KEY (its private key),
# DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS (the host key line, from the runbook's `ssh-keyscan`).

name: deploy

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      ref:
        description: ref to deploy (a branch or tag)
        default: main
        required: false

# One deploy at a time, and no cancel-in-progress: cancelling mid-ship would
# leave the host in a state nobody chose.
concurrency:
  group: deploy-production
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}
          # The gate scans the whole history (gitleaks), so the clone is
          # deep; a shallow one would scan one commit and pass vacuously.
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
          cache: true
      - name: gate
        run: make check
      - name: build
        run: CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -o dist/todo-server ./cmd/todo-server
      - name: install the key
        env:
          DEPLOY_SSH_KEY: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_SSH_KEY }}
          DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS }}
        run: |
          install -d -m 700 ~/.ssh
          printf '%s\n' "$DEPLOY_SSH_KEY" > ~/.ssh/deploy_key
          printf '%s\n' "$DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS" > ~/.ssh/known_hosts
          chmod 600 ~/.ssh/deploy_key ~/.ssh/known_hosts
      - name: ship
        env:
          DEPLOY_HOST: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_HOST }}
          DEPLOY_USER: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_USER }}
        run: |
          scp -i ~/.ssh/deploy_key dist/todo-server "$DEPLOY_USER@$DEPLOY_HOST:/tmp/todo-server.new"
      - name: install and restart
        env:
          DEPLOY_HOST: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_HOST }}
          DEPLOY_USER: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_USER }}
        run: |
          ssh -i ~/.ssh/deploy_key "$DEPLOY_USER@$DEPLOY_HOST" \
            'sudo install -m 0755 /tmp/todo-server.new /usr/local/bin/todo-server && rm -f /tmp/todo-server.new && sudo systemctl restart todo-server'
      - name: check
        env:
          DEPLOY_HOST: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_HOST }}
          DEPLOY_USER: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_USER }}
        run: |
          ssh -i ~/.ssh/deploy_key "$DEPLOY_USER@$DEPLOY_HOST" \
            'curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/ready'
````


## `.github/workflows/release.yml`

````yaml
# release.yml — the release: a v* tag is the decision, the workflow is the
# record, and what it leaves behind is a draft until a human publishes it.
# It takes effect once a remote exists; until then the file documents the
# pipeline, and `make release-check` is the same pipeline run by hand.
#
# The shape, and why:
#
#   - push on v* tags, not workflow_dispatch: a release is cut from a tag,
#     and the tag is the artifact's name. Nobody spells the version twice —
#     the tag is the version, and the workflow's trigger is the whole
#     filter.
#   - the gate runs first, the same one deploy.yml runs: the released
#     artifact is built from a tree the honesty machine passed. A tag can
#     point at a commit older than main's tip, so the gate re-checks the
#     tree the tag actually names.
#   - fetch-depth: 0: GoReleaser walks the history between the tag and the
#     previous one to write the changelog, and the gate's secrets scan
#     reads every commit — a shallow clone would quietly hollow out both.
#   - make release, not a bare goreleaser: the version pin lives in the
#     Makefile, once, and the workflow runs the same command a laptop runs.
#   - the login is the one thing the local run does not have: the image is
#     pushed to ghcr.io under the repository's own token. `make
#     release-check` skips the image when no container runtime is present.
#   - contents: write is the draft release and its artifacts; packages:
#     write is the image. Nothing else is asked of the token.
#   - the draft is the point of the last step: the tag can be pushed by a
#     machine, but the release is a decision, and a human reads the
#     changelog and checks the artifacts before the world does.

name: release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'

permissions:
  contents: write
  packages: write

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
          cache: true
      - name: gate
        run: make check
      - name: log in to the container registry
        run: echo "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" | docker login ghcr.io -u "${{ github.actor }}" --password-stdin
      - name: release
        run: make release
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
````

## `.golangci.yml`

````yaml
version: "2"

linters:
  # The curated gate: golangci-lint's five standard linters plus gosec.
  # `default: none` makes this list the whole policy: no linter is enabled by
  # accident, and a future tool release cannot add one behind our backs.
  default: none
  enable:
    - errcheck
    - govet
    - staticcheck
    - ineffassign
    - unused
    - gosec

  settings:
    staticcheck:
      # golangci-lint's staticcheck defaults leave the ST1xxx documentation
      # checks off; the audit turns them on, so a comment that no longer
      # matches its symbol — or an exported symbol without one — is a
      # finding, not a style opinion. The one report this produced is fixed
      # in internal/api: the session policy comment now leads with its
      # constructor.
      checks: ["all"]

    gosec:
      # gosec's whole rule set runs at the widest floors: no rule excluded
      # and nothing filtered by severity or confidence. The deliberate
      # exceptions live at the call site as `#nosec Gxxx -- reason`, and the
      # audit's suppression test (internal/audit) fails a directive without
      # a reason, so "deliberate" is enforced rather than asserted.
      severity: low
      confidence: low
      excludes: []

    errcheck:
      # errcheck layers its own built-in symbol exclusions on top of the
      # presets: fmt.Fprint* to os.Stderr, writes to bytes.Buffer and
      # strings.Builder, and a few hash/rand writes — calls whose error
      # cannot carry information the caller could act on. Kept (upstream
      # default) and made explicit; the arbitrary-io.Writer case is not on
      # that list, so it stays reported.
      disable-default-exclusions: false

  exclusions:
    # Generated files are not ours to fix. `strict` uses Go's own marker
    # (`// Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT.`, via ast.IsGenerated), which is
    # exactly what moq writes into store_moq_test.go.
    generated: strict

    # No exclusion presets, deliberately: v2 presets are opt-in (Default: []),
    # and the one that would matter here is std-error-handling (EXC0001). It
    # hides errcheck's report for any dropped fmt print/Close/Flush error by
    # name — but this CLI writes to an arbitrary io.Writer, and write
    # failures are part of run's error contract, so they must stay visible.
    presets: []
````


## `.goreleaser.yaml`

````yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://goreleaser.com/static/schema.json
#
# .goreleaser.yaml — the release plan: what a v* tag builds, archives,
# checksums, and drafts. `make release-check` runs the whole pipeline with
# --snapshot — no tag, no token, no publish — which is the dry run this
# chapter's gate is.
#
# The matrix is honest about what the engine can serve. The Turso driver
# calls a native library through purego, and the platform-libs module ships
# that library for exactly five targets: linux/amd64, linux/arm64,
# darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64, and windows/amd64. Two omissions are decisions
# chapter 20 measured, not oversights:
#
#   - windows/arm64: the build succeeds — the module's fallback is an empty
#     embed — and the binary fails at the first store open, with no engine
#     to extract. An artifact that cannot open its own database is not a
#     release target.
#   - 32-bit targets (386, arm): purego's fakecgo has no 32-bit
#     implementation, so the build fails inside the dependency, before any
#     code here compiles. They never enter the list; there is nothing to
#     exclude.
version: 2

project_name: todo

# Versioning: the release's name is its tag, and the tags are semver —
# vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. The app is pre-1.0 on purpose (v0.1.0 is the first
# release): the binaries' surface — the CLI's flags and JSON shapes, the
# HTTP API, the export format — can still move, and semver's pre-1.0 rule
# is that a breaking change bumps MINOR, not MAJOR. Once 1.0, the same
# change is a MAJOR. A -rc or -beta suffix makes a prerelease, and the
# release section below lets such a tag publish as one without a second
# switch to forget.

before:
  hooks:
    - go mod verify

builds:
  # One build per binary — the CLI, the server, and the TUI — and one shared
  # matrix: the anchor carries the settings all three agree on, and each
  # entry names only what differs. Every binary is stamped with the tag the
  # release was cut for; `todo version` prints it, the server and the TUI
  # record it at boot.
  - &build
    id: todo
    main: ./cmd/todo
    binary: todo
    env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0
    flags:
      - -trimpath
    ldflags:
      - -s -w -X todo/internal/version.Version={{ .Version }}
    goos:
      - linux
      - darwin
      - windows
    goarch:
      - amd64
      - arm64
    ignore:
      - goos: windows
        goarch: arm64
  - <<: *build
    id: todo-server
    main: ./cmd/todo-server
    binary: todo-server
  - <<: *build
    id: todo-tui
    main: ./cmd/todo-tui
    binary: todo-tui

archives:
  # One archive per platform, all three binaries inside: a release user
  # unpacks once and has the CLI, the server, and the TUI of the same build.
  # Windows gets a zip because it is the format Windows unpacks without a
  # second tool; the rest get the tarball every Unix already reads.
  - id: todo
    ids:
      - todo
      - todo-server
      - todo-tui
    formats:
      - tar.gz
    format_overrides:
      - goos: windows
        formats:
          - zip
    name_template: todo_{{ .Version }}_{{ .Os }}_{{ .Arch }}
    files:
      - README.md

checksum:
  name_template: checksums.txt

changelog:
  # The changelog is the tag's story, written from the local history the dry
  # run reads too: `use: git` needs no API, no token, and no tags on a
  # remote, so the workflow and a laptop generate the same notes. The groups
  # map onto the conventional prefixes the history already speaks, and the
  # bookkeeping commits — tests, chores — stay out: the release is for
  # readers, not for the repository's own trail.
  use: git
  sort: asc
  abbrev: -1
  groups:
    - title: Features
      regexp: '^feat(\(.+\))?!?:'
      order: 0
    - title: Fixes
      regexp: '^fix(\(.+\))?!?:'
      order: 1
    - title: Documentation
      regexp: '^docs(\(.+\))?!?:'
      order: 2
    - title: Others
      order: 999
  filters:
    exclude:
      - '^test(\(.+\))?!?:'
      - '^chore(\(.+\))?!?:'

release:
  # The tag is the decision; the release it leaves behind is a draft, and
  # publishing is the second, deliberate act. `prerelease: auto` keeps a
  # -rc or -beta tag a prerelease without a second switch to forget.
  draft: true
  prerelease: auto

dockers_v2:
  # One image, two platforms, one Dockerfile: the server binary on a
  # distroless base (deploy/Dockerfile carries the base-image reasoning).
  # GoReleaser feeds the per-platform binaries into the build context, so
  # nothing is built inside the Dockerfile — and the image work happens in
  # the publish phase, where a --snapshot run builds the images locally, one
  # per platform, and a release pushes the manifest.
  #
  # The image name is a placeholder: put your own registry namespace here,
  # and the release workflow's login step pushes it with the repository's
  # token. `latest` follows every non-prerelease tag, the way readers expect
  # a moving name to move.
  - images:
      - ghcr.io/your-org/todo-server
    ids:
      - todo-server
    tags:
      - "{{ .Version }}"
      - "{{ if not .Prerelease }}latest{{ end }}"
    dockerfile: deploy/Dockerfile
    platforms:
      - linux/amd64
      - linux/arm64
````


## `Makefile`

````makefile
# The local gate. CI runs the same targets, so a green run here is a green
# run there. Tool versions are pinned here, once.

GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION := v2.14.0
MOQ_VERSION           := v0.8.0
SQLC_VERSION          := v1.31.1
SWAG_VERSION          := v1.16.6
TEMPL_VERSION         := v0.3.1070

# The audit's three scanners, pinned like every other tool. gitleaks is
# required through its old module path on purpose: the project renamed to
# github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks, but the module's go.mod still declares
# github.com/zricethezav/gitleaks/v8, and `go run` resolves a tool by its
# declared path — the new path fails with "module declares its path as".
# syft is the heavyweight of the three: `go run` builds it from source,
# which is why `sbom` is a target of its own rather than part of check.
GITLEAKS_VERSION    := v8.30.1
GOVULNCHECK_VERSION := v1.9.0
SYFT_VERSION        := v1.54.1

# GoReleaser, pinned like every other tool — and pinned deliberately below
# the newest release: the v2.18 line's go.mod declares `go 1.27.x`, and this
# module's toolchain is 1.26.8, so `go run` refuses to build the tool at
# all. v2.17.1 is the newest release the pinned toolchain can run; the
# version moves when the Go directive does.
GORELEASER_VERSION := v2.17.1

# benchstat, for the benchmark gate's statistics and the bench target's human
# tables. The gate (cmd/benchgate) shells out to this pin: it builds the
# control revision's test binary and the working tree's, runs them
# alternately, and lets benchstat decide which differences the samples
# support. Nothing else in the module depends on golang.org/x/perf — the pin
# lives here, and the gate takes it as a flag so this stays the one place a
# tool version is written.
BENCHSTAT_VERSION := v0.0.0-20261009192801-be2c69fb417e

BENCHSTAT     := go run golang.org/x/perf/cmd/benchstat@$(BENCHSTAT_VERSION)

GITLEAKS      := go run github.com/zricethezav/gitleaks/v8@$(GITLEAKS_VERSION)
GOLANGCI_LINT := go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@$(GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION)
GORELEASER    := go run github.com/goreleaser/goreleaser/v2@$(GORELEASER_VERSION)
GOVULNCHECK   := go run golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@$(GOVULNCHECK_VERSION)
SWAG          := go run github.com/swaggo/swag/cmd/swag@$(SWAG_VERSION)
SYFT          := go run github.com/anchore/syft/cmd/syft@$(SYFT_VERSION)
TEMPL         := go run github.com/a-h/templ/cmd/templ@$(TEMPL_VERSION)

.PHONY: fmt vet test race lint vulncheck leaks sbom generate check schema-update bench bench-gate cover deploy-check release-check release

# fmt fails when any .go file is not gofmt-clean.
fmt:
	@unformatted="$$(gofmt -l .)"; \
	if [ -n "$$unformatted" ]; then \
		echo "gofmt would rewrite:"; echo "$$unformatted"; exit 1; \
	fi

vet:
	go vet ./...

test:
	go test -count=1 ./...

race:
	go test -race -count=1 ./...

lint:
	$(GOLANGCI_LINT) run

# vulncheck runs the Go vulnerability database over the module and reports
# what the code can reach. A module-level advisory for a package nothing
# imports is not a finding the gate can fix, and the tool's summary says so
# in its own words: symbol results, then package results, then module
# results. The database is fetched from vuln.go.dev on first run and cached.
vulncheck:
	$(GOVULNCHECK) ./...

# leaks scans the whole git history — every commit, not the working tree —
# for credentials. A key that reached a commit reached every clone, so the
# scan is over history, and the CI checkout is deep for the same reason.
leaks:
	$(GITLEAKS) git . --no-banner --no-color

# sbom writes the CycloneDX bill of materials the audit commits. It scans
# the repository's manifests: the Go module graph and the workflow's actions.
# The file catalogers are off (-file), so every component is a package purl
# and nothing carries the machine's own paths — that is what makes the
# committed document portable and what the SBOM test checks. Regenerating it
# is a deliberate act (syft is a heavyweight build, and the timestamp and
# serial change on every run), so this target is not part of check; the test
# in internal/audit is what keeps the committed copy honest.
sbom:
	$(SYFT) scan dir:. --source-name todo --select-catalogers=-file --quiet -o cyclonedx-json=docs/sbom.cdx.json

# generate runs every //go:generate directive in the module, then the swag
# pair and templ. The moq and sqlc versions in the directives are written
# literally: go generate expands environment variables ($VAR), never make
# variables, so $(MOQ_VERSION) or $(SQLC_VERSION) there would reach the tool
# as that literal text. The checks below keep each directive and its pin
# above in sync, and keep the query files ASCII: sqlc v1.31.1 counts token
# positions in runes but slices query text in bytes, so one multibyte
# character above a sqlc.slice query corrupts the generated text (reproduced
# with an em dash).
#
# swag is invoked from here rather than from a directive — its arguments are
# paths, and a directive in internal/api would have to spell them relative to
# that directory — so its pin lives only above. The check below keeps that pin
# and go.mod's github.com/swaggo/swag in sync: the generated docs.go imports
# the library, so the generator and the library must be the same version.
# swag fmt runs first, because swag init must generate from formatted
# annotations; a run that reformats anything leaves a diff for the staleness
# step in check to catch.
#
# templ is invoked from here for the same kind of reason: it walks the module
# for .templ files, and its generated _templ.go files import
# github.com/a-h/templ, so the check below keeps this pin and go.mod's in
# sync — a generator ahead of the library can emit code the library cannot
# compile. The .templ files and their generated Go live in internal/web.
generate:
	@pin="$$(grep -o 'matryer/moq@[^ ]*' internal/store/store.go || true)"; \
	if [ -n "$$pin" ] && [ "$$pin" != "matryer/moq@$(MOQ_VERSION)" ]; then \
		echo "internal/store/store.go pins $$pin; the Makefile pins matryer/moq@$(MOQ_VERSION)"; exit 1; \
	fi; \
	pin="$$(grep -o 'github.com/sqlc-dev/sqlc/cmd/sqlc@[^ ]*' internal/store/store.go || true)"; \
	if [ -n "$$pin" ] && [ "$$pin" != "github.com/sqlc-dev/sqlc/cmd/sqlc@$(SQLC_VERSION)" ]; then \
		echo "internal/store/store.go pins $$pin; the Makefile pins github.com/sqlc-dev/sqlc/cmd/sqlc@$(SQLC_VERSION)"; exit 1; \
	fi; \
	pin="$$(grep -o 'github.com/swaggo/swag v[^ ]*' go.mod || true)"; \
	if [ -n "$$pin" ] && [ "$$pin" != "github.com/swaggo/swag $(SWAG_VERSION)" ]; then \
		echo "go.mod pins $$pin; the Makefile pins github.com/swaggo/swag $(SWAG_VERSION)"; exit 1; \
	fi; \
	pin="$$(grep -o 'github.com/a-h/templ v[^ ]*' go.mod || true)"; \
	if [ -n "$$pin" ] && [ "$$pin" != "github.com/a-h/templ $(TEMPL_VERSION)" ]; then \
		echo "go.mod pins $$pin; the Makefile pins github.com/a-h/templ $(TEMPL_VERSION)"; exit 1; \
	fi; \
	nonascii="$$(grep -rlP '[^\x00-\x7F]' internal/db/queries || true)"; \
	if [ -n "$$nonascii" ]; then \
		echo "sqlc reads these files; keep them ASCII:"; echo "$$nonascii"; exit 1; \
	fi
	go generate ./...
	$(TEMPL) generate
	$(SWAG) fmt -d cmd/todo-server,internal/api -g main.go
	$(SWAG) init -g cmd/todo-server/main.go -o internal/api/docs --parseInternal

# check is the full local gate: format, vet, lint, the two scanners — the
# vulnerability database and the history's secrets — regenerate — failing if
# that changed anything, because generated code must be committed — then
# test. The schema golden is part of the test step: TestMigratedSchemaMatchesGolden
# compares the migrated schema with internal/db/schema.sql, and schema-update
# below regenerates that file.
check: fmt vet lint vulncheck leaks generate
	@git diff --exit-code || { echo "generated files are stale: run make generate and commit"; exit 1; }
	go test -count=1 ./...

# deploy-check is the deploy dry run: the parts of the deployment that can be
# checked on this machine. systemd-analyze parses the unit files offline —
# no manager needed — and scores the server unit's hardening; the committed
# files name the installed paths, so the check runs on copies with ExecStart
# and the credential path rewritten into a scratch directory (the rewrite is
# the one difference from what the chapter committed). The threshold is the
# score the chapter earned, with room for a systemd version's scoring drift:
# 1.5 exposed is 15%, and the gate refuses over 25%. The drain and the backup
# contracts are the tests the chapter added, run by name so the deploy gate
# is one command.
deploy-check:
	@command -v systemd-analyze >/dev/null || { echo "deploy-check needs systemd-analyze"; exit 1; }
	@tmp="$$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$$tmp"' EXIT; \
	go build -o "$$tmp/todo-server" ./cmd/todo-server; \
	install -m 0400 /dev/null "$$tmp/admin-key"; \
	install -D -m 0755 deploy/todo-backup.sh "$$tmp/todo-backup"; \
	sed -e "s|/usr/local/bin/todo-server|$$tmp/todo-server|" \
	    -e "s|/etc/todo/admin-key|$$tmp/admin-key|" \
	    deploy/todo-server.service > "$$tmp/todo-server.service"; \
	sed -e "s|/usr/local/lib/todo/todo-backup|$$tmp/todo-backup|" \
	    -e "s|/usr/local/bin/todo|$$tmp/todo-server|" \
	    deploy/todo-backup.service > "$$tmp/todo-backup.service"; \
	cp deploy/todo-backup.timer "$$tmp/todo-backup.timer"; \
	systemd-analyze verify "$$tmp/todo-server.service" "$$tmp/todo-backup.service" "$$tmp/todo-backup.timer"; \
	systemd-analyze security --offline=yes --threshold=25 "$$tmp/todo-server.service" | tail -1
	go test -count=1 -run 'TestGracefulShutdown_Drains|TestBackupScript_Restores' ./cmd/todo-server

# release-check is the release dry run: the whole matrix built, archived,
# and checksummed into dist/ with no tag, no token, and no publish — the
# same pipeline the release workflow runs, minus the two things a laptop
# cannot give it. One of those is the image: the docker phase needs a
# container runtime, and when none is present it is skipped with the reason
# printed rather than failing the gate. The other is the git state: with no
# remote, GoReleaser's git pipe falls back to its fake snapshot info, so the
# dry-run artifacts carry 0.0.0-SNAPSHOT-none and an empty changelog — the
# pipeline is exercised, the version is the tool's placeholder, and the
# notes say so.
release-check:
	@if docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
		$(GORELEASER) release --snapshot --clean; \
	else \
		echo "release-check: no container runtime; skipping the image phase (--skip=docker)"; \
		$(GORELEASER) release --snapshot --clean --skip=docker; \
	fi

# release is the real thing: a tagged commit and GITHUB_TOKEN in the
# environment, leaving a draft on the release page for a human to publish.
# The release workflow runs exactly this target, so the local and the CI
# runs are one command.
release:
	$(GORELEASER) release --clean

# schema-update rewrites the schema golden from the embedded migrations, for
# the one case the drift check cannot decide for you: a schema change you
# made on purpose.
schema-update:
	UPDATE_SCHEMA=1 go test -run TestMigratedSchemaMatchesGolden ./internal/db

bench:
	go test -bench=. -benchmem -count=10 ./internal/store

# bench-gate is the performance gate: the working tree's benchmarks, run
# alternately with a test binary built from the revision each committed
# baseline names in its "# control-ref:" header line, compared by benchstat
# and judged by the policy in internal/benchgate (no extra allocations, no
# more than 5% more bytes, no more than 25% more time, and nothing at all for
# a difference the samples cannot separate from noise).
#
# The two-binary shape is chapter 12's interleaving method, executable: the
# comparison happens inside one session, on one machine, so load, frequency,
# and thermal state are shared and the gate does not depend on where it runs.
# The price is the build: each gate run compiles the control revision's test
# binaries as well as the current ones. It is minutes, not seconds, which is
# why it is its own target and a CI job of its own — not part of check.
bench-gate:
	go run ./cmd/benchgate -benchstat='$(BENCHSTAT)' ./internal/store ./internal/web ./internal/api

cover:
	go test -count=1 -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...
	go tool cover -func=coverage.out | tail -1
````


## `README.md`

````markdown
# todo — the reference application

The finished todo application from the book **Build a Todo App in Go** — the
tree every quote and transcript in the book was captured from.

It is not a starter project: the book carries the finished tree in full in
its reference appendix, and readers build their own from chapter one.
````


## `cmd/benchgate/main.go`

````go
// Command benchgate is the benchmark regression gate: it builds the test
// binaries of two revisions — the one a committed baseline names in its
// `# control-ref:` header line, and the working tree — runs them alternately
// against the same workload, and fails when the current tree is slower than
// the control by more than the policy allows.
//
// The two-binary shape is chapter 12's interleaving method made executable.
// A gate that compares a fresh run against committed numbers is comparing
// two sessions: the machine's load, frequency, and thermal state move the
// numbers by more than most regressions do, and no statistic can see that
// from the samples. Running both revisions in the same session, alternately,
// gives them the same conditions — and it makes the gate portable: it does
// not matter which machine it runs on, because both sides ran there.
//
// What is gated, and how, is internal/benchgate's policy: zero tolerance for
// extra allocations, five percent for bytes, twenty-five percent for time,
// and nothing at all for a difference benchstat's test cannot separate from
// noise.
//
// Usage:
//
//	go run ./cmd/benchgate -benchstat='go run golang.org/x/perf/cmd/benchstat@vX' ./internal/store ./internal/web ./internal/api
//
// Each package is gated against every baseline file under
// <pkg>/testdata/bench/ that carries a `# control-ref: <rev>` header line; a
// baseline without one is a record, reported and skipped. -update rewrites
// those files with a fresh run and the current revision as the new control.
package main

import (
	"archive/tar"
	"bytes"
	"errors"
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"slices"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"todo/internal/benchgate"
)

func main() {
	err := run()
	switch {
	case err == nil:
		return
	case errors.Is(err, errRegression):
		// The gate ran and found a regression: exit 1, which is what a CI
		// step and a human both read as "the tree is worse".
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "benchgate:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	default:
		// The gate could not run — a usage error, a missing revision, a
		// build that failed. Exit 125, git bisect's "skip this commit":
		// a predicate that cannot run must not report the commit as bad,
		// or bisect blames whatever it tested while the gate was broken.
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "benchgate:", err)
		os.Exit(125)
	}
}

// options is the gate's configuration, assembled from the flags.
type options struct {
	pkgs      []string
	count     int
	bench     string
	benchstat string
	control   string
	update    bool
	keep      bool
	policy    benchgate.Policy
}

// controlPrefix marks the header line a gated baseline carries: the revision
// whose test binary the gate builds as the comparison's control.
const controlPrefix = "# control-ref: "

// errNoBenchMatch reports that a -bench pattern selects none of a suite's
// benchmarks, which is a skip for that suite, not a failure of the gate.
var errNoBenchMatch = errors.New("no benchmark matches -bench")

// errRegression is the gate's verdict: the tree is worse than the control by
// more than the policy allows. Every other error is "the gate could not
// run", which exits differently on purpose (see main).
var errRegression = errors.New("the gate found a regression")

// parseFlags reads the command line.
func parseFlags(args []string) (options, error) {
	var opts options
	fs := flag.NewFlagSet("benchgate", flag.ContinueOnError)
	fs.Func("pkg", "package to gate (repeatable; default ./internal/store, ./internal/web, ./internal/api)", func(pkg string) error {
		opts.pkgs = append(opts.pkgs, pkg)
		return nil
	})
	fs.IntVar(&opts.count, "count", 5, "samples per side")
	fs.StringVar(&opts.bench, "bench", "", "extra benchmark filter, on top of each baseline's own names")
	fs.StringVar(&opts.benchstat, "benchstat", "", "benchstat invocation, such as 'go run golang.org/x/perf/cmd/benchstat@vX.Y.Z' (required)")
	fs.StringVar(&opts.control, "control", "", "override the control revision (default: each baseline's # control-ref)")
	fs.BoolVar(&opts.update, "update", false, "rewrite the gated baselines with a fresh run and the current revision as the control")
	fs.BoolVar(&opts.keep, "keep", false, "keep the gate's scratch directory (it prints the path)")
	fs.Float64Var(&opts.policy.Allocs, "allocs", 0, "largest tolerated allocs/op regression, as a fraction (negative disables)")
	fs.Float64Var(&opts.policy.Bytes, "bytes", 0.05, "largest tolerated B/op regression, as a fraction (negative disables)")
	fs.Float64Var(&opts.policy.Secs, "secs", 0.25, "largest tolerated sec/op regression, as a fraction (negative disables)")
	if err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil {
		return options{}, err
	}
	if len(opts.pkgs) == 0 {
		opts.pkgs = []string{"./internal/store", "./internal/web", "./internal/api"}
	}
	if opts.benchstat == "" {
		return options{}, fmt.Errorf("-benchstat is required; the Makefile pins it (see make bench-gate)")
	}
	// benchstat's test over n samples a side cannot return a p-value below
	// 2/(n(n+1)) — with three samples that is 0.1, so no difference could
	// ever clear a 0.05 alpha and the time half of the gate would be dead.
	// Four is the smallest count that can say "significant".
	if opts.count < 4 {
		return options{}, fmt.Errorf("-count %d is too few: benchstat cannot reach p<0.05 with fewer than 4 samples per side", opts.count)
	}
	opts.policy.Alpha = benchgate.DefaultPolicy().Alpha
	return opts, nil
}

// suite is one baseline file: the benchmark names it holds, the filter that
// selects them, and the control revision it names.
type suite struct {
	pkg      string
	path     string
	names    []string
	filter   string
	control  string
	recorded bool // carries a control-ref header
}

func run() error {
	opts, err := parseFlags(os.Args[1:])
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := ensureRepo(); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	tmp, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "benchgate-*")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if opts.keep {
		fmt.Printf("scratch: %s\n", tmp)
	} else {
		defer func() { _ = os.RemoveAll(tmp) }()
	}

	failed := false
	for _, pkg := range opts.pkgs {
		ok, err := gatePackage(opts, pkg, tmp)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", pkg, err)
		}
		if !ok {
			failed = true
		}
	}
	if failed {
		return errRegression
	}
	fmt.Println("benchgate: pass")
	return nil
}

// gatePackage gates one package: it reads the package's baselines, builds the
// control and current test binaries, runs the interleaved capture, and prints
// the verdict.
func gatePackage(opts options, pkg, tmp string) (bool, error) {
	suites, err := readSuites(pkg)
	if err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	gated := slices.DeleteFunc(slices.Clone(suites), func(s suite) bool { return !s.recorded })
	for _, s := range suites {
		if !s.recorded {
			fmt.Printf("%s: %s is a record, not gated (no %q line)\n", pkg, s.path, strings.TrimSpace(controlPrefix))
		}
	}
	if len(gated) == 0 {
		fmt.Printf("%s: nothing to gate\n", pkg)
		return true, nil
	}

	control := opts.control
	if control == "" {
		for _, s := range gated {
			if s.control == "" {
				return false, fmt.Errorf("%s names no control", s.path)
			}
		}
	}

	controls := map[string]string{}
	controlFor := func(s suite) (string, string, error) {
		rev := control
		if rev == "" {
			rev = s.control
		}
		if bin, ok := controls[rev]; ok {
			return bin, rev, nil
		}
		bin, err := buildControl(opts, pkg, rev, tmp)
		if err != nil {
			return "", "", err
		}
		controls[rev] = bin
		return bin, rev, nil
	}
	currentBin, err := buildCurrent(opts, pkg, tmp)
	if err != nil {
		return false, err
	}

	fmt.Printf("bench gate: %s (%d samples per side)\n", pkg, opts.count)
	if opts.update {
		return true, updateSuites(opts, gated, currentBin, tmp)
	}

	ok := true
	for _, s := range gated {
		controlBin, rev, err := controlFor(s)
		if err != nil {
			return false, err
		}
		fmt.Printf("\n  %s (control %s)\n", s.path, rev)
		controlOut := filepath.Join(tmp, strings.ReplaceAll(s.path, string(filepath.Separator), "_")+".control")
		currentOut := controlOut + ".current"
		if err := capture(opts, controlBin, currentBin, s, controlOut, currentOut, tmp); err != nil {
			if errors.Is(err, errNoBenchMatch) {
				fmt.Printf("  skipped: no benchmark matches -bench %q\n", opts.bench)
				continue
			}
			return false, err
		}
		if empty(controlOut) {
			fmt.Printf("  no comparable rows: the control does not run this suite's benchmarks\n")
			continue
		}
		verdict, err := compare(opts, controlOut, currentOut)
		if err != nil {
			return false, err
		}
		report(verdict, opts.policy)
		if !verdict.OK() {
			ok = false
		}
	}
	return ok, nil
}

// empty reports whether a capture holds no benchmark lines, which is what a
// control revision that predates the suite produces.
func empty(path string) bool {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path) // #nosec G304 -- the path is the gate's own capture file in its scratch directory
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	return !strings.Contains(string(data), "Benchmark")
}

// capture runs the two binaries alternately, one round each per sample, so
// every pair of samples shares the machine's conditions. Each side gets one
// discarded warm-up round first: the first benchmark in a process pays for
// lazy page loads and the seeded database's first touch, and neither side
// should carry that alone.
func capture(opts options, controlBin, currentBin string, s suite, controlOut, currentOut, tmp string) error {
	filter := s.filter
	if opts.bench != "" {
		// -bench narrows the suite: a focused run — the bisect predicate, a
		// single suspicious benchmark — selects the names the pattern
		// matches. A suite with no matching names is skipped by the caller.
		re, err := regexp.Compile(opts.bench)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("-bench %q: %w", opts.bench, err)
		}
		var names []string
		for _, name := range s.names {
			if re.MatchString(name) {
				names = append(names, name)
			}
		}
		if len(names) == 0 {
			return errNoBenchMatch
		}
		filter = nameFilter(names)
	}
	run := func(bin, side string, out io.Writer) error {
		return runBench(bin, filter, filepath.Join(tmp, side+".db"), out)
	}
	appendRun := func(bin, side, out string) error {
		f, err := os.OpenFile(out, os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY|os.O_APPEND, 0o600) // #nosec G304 -- the path is the gate's own capture file in its scratch directory
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
		return run(bin, side, f)
	}
	if err := run(controlBin, "control", io.Discard); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := run(currentBin, "current", io.Discard); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	for i := 0; i < opts.count; i++ {
		if err := appendRun(controlBin, "control", controlOut); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if err := appendRun(currentBin, "current", currentOut); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// compare runs benchstat over the two captures and applies the policy.
func compare(opts options, controlOut, currentOut string) (benchgate.Verdict, error) {
	args := append(strings.Fields(opts.benchstat), "-format", "csv", controlOut, currentOut)
	cmd := exec.Command(args[0], args[1:]...) // #nosec G204 -- the command is the benchstat pin the Makefile passes, and the paths are the gate's own captures
	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
	cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		return benchgate.Verdict{}, fmt.Errorf("benchstat: %w: %s", err, strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String()))
	}
	return benchgate.Compare(&stdout, opts.policy)
}

// report prints one suite's table and its failures.
func report(verdict benchgate.Verdict, policy benchgate.Policy) {
	var metric benchgate.Metric
	for _, row := range verdict.Rows {
		if row.Metric != metric {
			metric = row.Metric
			fmt.Printf("  %s\n", metric)
		}
		delta := benchgate.FormatPercent(row.Delta)
		mark := " "
		if !row.Significant {
			mark = "~"
		} else if budget, gated := policy.Budget(row.Metric); gated && row.Delta > budget {
			mark = "!"
		}
		fmt.Printf("  %s %-46s %14s -> %-14s %9s  %s\n", mark, row.Benchmark,
			benchgate.FormatValue(row.Metric, row.Control), benchgate.FormatValue(row.Metric, row.Current), delta, row.P)
	}
	for _, f := range verdict.Failures {
		fmt.Printf("\n  FAIL %s %s: %s (budget %s)\n", f.Row.Benchmark, f.Row.Metric,
			benchgate.FormatPercent(f.Row.Delta), benchgate.FormatPercent(f.Budget))
	}
}

// updateSuites rewrites each gated baseline with a fresh run and the current
// revision as its control. The run is the same shape a gate run captures: one
// discarded warm-up, then -count samples — a baseline recorded from one cold
// sample would be a weaker floor than the gate it exists for.
func updateSuites(opts options, suites []suite, currentBin, tmp string) error {
	rev, err := git("rev-parse", "HEAD")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	rev = strings.TrimSpace(rev)
	for _, s := range suites {
		if err := runBench(currentBin, s.filter, filepath.Join(tmp, "update.db"), io.Discard); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		var out bytes.Buffer
		for i := 0; i < opts.count; i++ {
			if err := runBench(currentBin, s.filter, filepath.Join(tmp, "update.db"), &out); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
		body := out.String()
		at := strings.Index(body, "\nBenchmark")
		if at < 0 {
			return fmt.Errorf("%s: the fresh run reported no benchmarks", s.path)
		}
		body = body[:at+1] + controlPrefix + rev + "\n" + body[at+1:]
		if err := os.WriteFile(s.path, []byte(body), 0o600); err != nil { // #nosec G306 -- a baseline is a record, and 0600 is what the committed one carries
			return err
		}
		fmt.Printf("updated %s (control %s, %d samples)\n", s.path, rev, opts.count)
	}
	return nil
}

// readSuites reads a package's baseline files.
func readSuites(pkg string) ([]suite, error) {
	dir := filepath.Join(strings.TrimPrefix(pkg, "./"), "testdata", "bench")
	paths, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(dir, "*.txt"))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if len(paths) == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no baselines under %s", dir)
	}
	var suites []suite
	for _, path := range paths {
		data, err := os.ReadFile(path) // #nosec G304 -- the path is a baseline under the package's testdata directory, found by glob
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		s := suite{pkg: pkg, path: path}
		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(data), "\n") {
			switch {
			case strings.HasPrefix(line, controlPrefix):
				s.control = strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(line, controlPrefix))
				s.recorded = true
			case strings.HasPrefix(line, "Benchmark"):
				s.names = append(s.names, benchmarkName(line))
			}
		}
		s.filter = nameFilter(s.names)
		suites = append(suites, s)
	}
	return suites, nil
}

// benchmarkName strips the -N GOMAXPROCS suffix from a benchmark output line,
// leaving the name a -bench filter matches.
func benchmarkName(line string) string {
	name := strings.Fields(line)[0]
	if i := strings.LastIndex(name, "-"); i > 0 {
		if _, err := strconv.Atoi(name[i+1:]); err == nil {
			return name[:i]
		}
	}
	return name
}

// nameFilter builds the -bench pattern that selects the given benchmark
// names. The pattern names top-level benchmarks only — the part before the
// first slash — because testing splits a filter on unbracketed slashes and
// matches each part against one element of a benchmark's name: a pattern that
// spells a sub-name cannot also be an alternation of whole names. Selecting
// the top level runs every sub-benchmark of a selected name, which is what a
// suite wants: the baseline's sub-names are compared, and a sub-benchmark the
// control did not have is reported unpaired rather than silently skipped.
func nameFilter(names []string) string {
	seen := make(map[string]bool, len(names))
	var parts []string
	for _, name := range names {
		top, _, _ := strings.Cut(name, "/")
		if seen[top] {
			continue
		}
		seen[top] = true
		parts = append(parts, regexp.QuoteMeta(top))
	}
	return "^(" + strings.Join(parts, "|") + ")$"
}

// buildControl extracts the control revision and builds its test binary for
// the package. The tree arrives through git archive rather than a worktree:
// the gate reads history, it does not create state in the repository.
func buildControl(opts options, pkg, rev, tmp string) (string, error) {
	dir := filepath.Join(tmp, "control-"+sanitize(rev))
	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o750); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if err := extract(rev, dir); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	bin := filepath.Join(tmp, "control-"+sanitize(pkg)+".test")
	return bin, buildTest(dir, pkg, bin)
}

// buildCurrent builds the working tree's test binary for the package.
func buildCurrent(opts options, pkg, tmp string) (string, error) {
	bin := filepath.Join(tmp, "current-"+sanitize(pkg)+".test")
	return bin, buildTest(".", pkg, bin)
}

// buildTest compiles a package's test binary in dir.
func buildTest(dir, pkg, out string) error {
	cmd := exec.Command("go", "test", "-c", "-o", out, pkg) // #nosec G204 -- pkg is a package path from the gate's own flags, and out is in its scratch directory
	cmd.Dir = dir
	cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("go test -c %s: %w", pkg, err)
	}
	return nil
}

// runBench runs one test binary's benchmarks into out. A benchmark run's
// tests are skipped: the gate measures, it does not test.
func runBench(bin, filter, dbPath string, out io.Writer) error {
	cmd := exec.Command(bin, // #nosec G204 -- bin is a test binary the gate just built in its scratch directory
		"-test.run=^$",
		"-test.bench="+filter,
		"-test.benchmem",
		"-test.count=1",
		"-test.timeout=60m",
	)
	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "TODO_PERF_DB="+dbPath)
	cmd.Stdout = out
	cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("run %s: %w", filepath.Base(bin), err)
	}
	return nil
}

// extract writes the revision's tree into dir through git archive.
func extract(rev, dir string) error {
	cmd := exec.Command("git", "archive", "--format=tar", rev) // #nosec G204 -- rev is a baseline's control ref, read from a committed file
	stdout, err := cmd.StdoutPipe()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
	if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("git archive %s: %w", rev, err)
	}
	tr := tar.NewReader(stdout)
	for {
		hdr, err := tr.Next()
		if err == io.EOF {
			break
		}
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		path := filepath.Join(dir, filepath.FromSlash(hdr.Name))
		switch hdr.Typeflag {
		case tar.TypeDir:
			if err := os.MkdirAll(path, 0o750); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		case tar.TypeReg:
			if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o750); err != nil {
				return err
			}
			perm := hdr.Mode & 0o777
			// #nosec G304 -- the path comes from the archive of the gate's own control revision
			// #nosec G115 -- perm is masked to permission bits above
			f, err := os.OpenFile(path, os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY|os.O_TRUNC, os.FileMode(perm))
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			if _, err := io.Copy(f, tr); err != nil { // #nosec G110 -- the stream is this repository's own git archive, not untrusted input
				_ = f.Close()
				return err
			}
			if err := f.Close(); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
	}
	if err := cmd.Wait(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("git archive %s: %w", rev, err)
	}
	return nil
}

// git runs one git command in the repository and returns its stdout.
func git(args ...string) (string, error) {
	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
	cmd := exec.Command("git", args...) // #nosec G204 -- the gate's own git calls, with arguments built in this file
	cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("git %s: %w: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), err, strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String()))
	}
	return stdout.String(), nil
}

// ensureRepo fails early and clearly when the gate is run outside a git
// repository, which is where the control revision lives.
func ensureRepo() error {
	if _, err := git("rev-parse", "--git-dir"); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("benchgate needs a git repository: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}

// sanitize turns a path or revision into a file name.
func sanitize(s string) string {
	return strings.NewReplacer("/", "_", ".", "_", ":", "_").Replace(s)
}
````


## `cmd/todo-server/backup_test.go`

````go
// The backup job's contract: deploy/todo-backup.sh runs against a live
// server's database — while the sidecar log holds everything the .db file
// does not — and the copy it writes opens in a scratch store with the tasks
// the server held. The restore is the assertion that matters: a copy that
// lost the sidecars opens perfectly well and holds nothing, so "it opened"
// is not the test.
package main

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/google/uuid"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"todo/internal/store"
)

// backupScript is the job the timer runs, as this package's directory sees
// it.
const backupScript = "../../deploy/todo-backup.sh"

// buildCLI builds the todo CLI — the script's verification tool — into dir
// and returns its path.
func buildCLI(t *testing.T, dir string) string {
	t.Helper()

	bin := filepath.Join(dir, "todo")
	// #nosec G204 -- the command is a literal; only the output path, chosen
	// by the test, varies.
	cmd := exec.Command("go", "build", "-o", bin, "todo/cmd/todo")
	cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
	require.NoError(t, cmd.Run(), "build the todo CLI")
	return bin
}

// TestBackupScript_Restores runs the backup job the way the timer does —
// against a server that is up and holding its database open — and restores
// the copy into a scratch store: the copy must open and hold the tasks that
// were created through the API, which live in the sidecar log until a
// checkpoint folds them into the .db file.
func TestBackupScript_Restores(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	srv := startServer(t)
	defer srv.stop(t)

	base := "http://" + srv.addr

	// A user and two tasks, through the real routes: rows the .db file
	// alone would not have while the server runs.
	resp := postJSON(t, base+"/api/v1/auth/register", `{"email":"backup@example.com","password":"correct horse battery staple"}`, nil)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, resp.StatusCode)
	var registered struct {
		ID string `json:"id"`
	}
	require.NoError(t, json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&registered))
	require.NoError(t, resp.Body.Close())
	owner, err := uuid.Parse(registered.ID)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	resp = postJSON(t, base+"/api/v1/auth/login", `{"email":"backup@example.com","password":"correct horse battery staple"}`, nil)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, resp.StatusCode)
	cookies := resp.Cookies()
	require.NoError(t, resp.Body.Close())
	require.Len(t, cookies, 1, "login sets the session cookie")

	for _, title := range []string{"buy milk", "walk the dog"} {
		resp = postJSON(t, base+"/api/v1/tasks", `{"title":"`+title+`"}`, func(req *http.Request) {
			req.AddCookie(cookies[0])
		})
		require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, resp.StatusCode, "create %q", title)
		require.NoError(t, resp.Body.Close())
	}

	// The job, with the paths the unit would set: the live database, a
	// scratch backup directory, and the CLI for the verification.
	backupDir := t.TempDir()
	script := exec.Command("sh", backupScript)
	script.Env = []string{
		"PATH=" + os.Getenv("PATH"),
		"TODO_DB=" + filepath.Join(srv.dir, "todo.db"),
		"TODO_BACKUP_DIR=" + backupDir,
		"TODO_BIN=" + buildCLI(t, t.TempDir()),
	}
	out, err := script.CombinedOutput()
	require.NoError(t, err, "the backup job failed:\n%s", out)

	copies, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(backupDir, "todo-*.db"))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Len(t, copies, 1, "one copy per run; the directory holds:\n%s", out)

	// The verification's own open folds the sidecars into the copy: the log
	// the script copied is left truncated, so what the backup directory holds
	// is one portable file plus the empty sidecar the engine keeps. A copy
	// whose log still held bytes would mean the verification never ran.
	if info, err := os.Stat(copies[0] + "-log"); err == nil {
		assert.Zero(t, info.Size(), "the verification's open folds the log into the copy")
	}

	// The restore: the copy opened in a scratch store, scoped to the user
	// whose tasks it must hold.
	ctx := context.Background()
	restored, err := store.NewTursoStore(ctx, copies[0])
	require.NoError(t, err, "the copy opens")
	defer func() { require.NoError(t, restored.Close()) }()

	tasks, err := restored.Scoped(owner).List(ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	titles := make([]string, 0, len(tasks))
	for _, task := range tasks {
		titles = append(titles, task.Title)
	}
	assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{"buy milk", "walk the dog"}, titles,
		"the copy holds every task the live database held; stderr:\n%s", srv.stderr.String())
}
````


## `cmd/todo-server/drain_test.go`

````go
// The drain cases: chapter 48's contract for what a SIGTERM does to a
// running server. The in-flight request is held open at the transport level —
// the head and half the body arrive, so the handler parks in the body read —
// because a request that has not started cannot be in flight when the signal
// arrives, and a request that has finished proves nothing.
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net"
	"strings"
	"syscall"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// holdRequest opens a request that stops mid-body: the head and half the body
// are written, so the handler is inside the body read — an active request, by
// net/http's own connection accounting — when the test signals the process.
// The returned function writes the rest and reads the response, and the
// connection stays open until then, so the drain has something to wait for.
func holdRequest(t *testing.T, addr, path string, body []byte) (net.Conn, func() string) {
	t.Helper()

	conn, err := net.Dial("tcp", addr)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	half := len(body) / 2
	head := fmt.Sprintf("POST %s HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: %s\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: %d\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n",
		path, addr, len(body))
	_, err = conn.Write(append([]byte(head), body[:half]...))
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// The server must have read the head before the signal: a connection it
	// has not read from is still "new" to net/http, and Shutdown closes new
	// connections as idle. The sleep is the only lever a black-box test has
	// for that state; the handler then blocks in the body read for as long
	// as the test keeps the rest unwritten.
	time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond)

	return conn, func() string {
		t.Helper()
		_, err := conn.Write(body[half:])
		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.NoError(t, conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(10*time.Second)))
		raw, err := io.ReadAll(conn)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.NoError(t, conn.Close())
		status, _, _ := strings.Cut(string(raw), "\r\n")
		return status
	}
}

// waitForRecord polls the captured stderr for want: the lifecycle record is
// the process's own statement that the signal was received and the drain is
// under way, so a case synchronizes on it instead of sleeping.
func waitForRecord(t *testing.T, out *syncBuffer, want string) {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)
	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
		if strings.Contains(out.String(), want) {
			return
		}
		time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
	}
	t.Fatalf("no %q record; stderr:\n%s", want, out.String())
}

// TestGracefulShutdown_Drains is the chapter's drain contract, in the three
// properties a service manager depends on: a signal stops the process
// accepting while an in-flight request finishes and the process then exits
// clean; the drain budget outlasts the request deadline the stack itself
// arms, so a request the server would still have served is not cut by the
// drain; and a second signal is the operator's escape hatch when a drain
// hangs — the shape systemd's own two-stage stop has one level up.
func TestGracefulShutdown_Drains(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("an in-flight request completes", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		srv := startServer(t)
		body := []byte(`{"email":"drain@example.com","password":"correct horse battery staple"}`)
		_, finish := holdRequest(t, srv.addr, "/api/v1/auth/register", body)

		require.NoError(t, srv.cmd.Process.Signal(syscall.SIGTERM))
		waitForRecord(t, srv.stderr, `"msg":"shutting down"`)

		// The request was in flight when the signal arrived; its body
		// finishes now, during the drain, and the response must arrive
		// whole — 201, the registration's own status.
		assert.Contains(t, finish(), "201 Created")

		select {
		case err := <-srv.wait:
			require.NoError(t, err, "a drained process exits 0; stderr:\n%s", srv.stderr.String())
		case <-time.After(10 * time.Second):
			_ = srv.cmd.Process.Kill()
			<-srv.wait
			t.Fatal("the server did not exit after the drain")
		}
	})

	t.Run("a second signal is the operator's escape hatch", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		srv := startServer(t)
		body := []byte(`{"email":"stuck@example.com","password":"correct horse battery staple"}`)
		conn, _ := holdRequest(t, srv.addr, "/api/v1/auth/register", body)
		// The request never finishes; the drain has no way out on its own.
		defer func() { _ = conn.Close() }()

		require.NoError(t, srv.cmd.Process.Signal(syscall.SIGTERM))
		waitForRecord(t, srv.stderr, `"msg":"shutting down"`)

		// The first signal started a drain that will wait out the whole
		// budget for a request that is never going to finish. The second
		// signal must end the process now — and by signal, not by a clean
		// drain: the operator asked for it, and a systemd unit watching
		// the exit code must be able to tell the difference.
		require.NoError(t, srv.cmd.Process.Signal(syscall.SIGTERM))
		select {
		case <-srv.wait:
			ws, ok := srv.cmd.ProcessState.Sys().(syscall.WaitStatus)
			require.True(t, ok, "wait status")
			assert.True(t, ws.Signaled(), "the second signal must end the process, not be swallowed")
			assert.Equal(t, syscall.SIGTERM, ws.Signal())
		case <-time.After(3 * time.Second):
			_ = srv.cmd.Process.Kill()
			<-srv.wait
			t.Fatal("a second SIGTERM did not end the drain")
		}
	})

	t.Run("the drain budget outlasts the request deadline", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		// internal/api arms a ten-second deadline on every request (its
		// requestTimeout); a request that was in flight when the signal
		// arrived can have that whole deadline left to run. A drain budget
		// below it cuts work the stack would still have served — and exits
		// non-zero, which a supervisor reads as a failed stop.
		assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, shutdownTimeout, 10*time.Second,
			"the drain must outlast internal/api's request deadline")
	})
}
````


## `cmd/todo-server/integration_test.go`

````go
// The black-box test: the real server binary TestMain built, run through
// exec.Command with a deliberately bare environment. testscript cannot
// background a long-running server — its scripts run commands to completion —
// so this package drives the process directly: start, poll, signal, wait,
// the way a service manager would.
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"syscall"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// binPath is the server binary TestMain builds once for the tests below;
// binDir is the temporary directory holding it, removed after the suite.
var (
	binPath string
	binDir  string
)

// TestMain builds the real binary once, runs the suite, and removes the
// binary's directory. Unlike cmd/todo's, this TestMain has no testscript
// commands to register: the server is only ever exercised as a process.
func TestMain(m *testing.M) {
	if err := buildBinary(); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	code := m.Run()
	if binDir != "" {
		if err := os.RemoveAll(binDir); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "remove test binary dir:", err)
		}
	}
	os.Exit(code)
}

// buildBinary builds the server once for the whole suite. `go test` runs
// this binary with the package directory as the working directory, so `.` is
// cmd/todo-server.
func buildBinary() error {
	dir, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "todo-server-bin-")
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("build test binary: %w", err)
	}
	binDir = dir
	binPath = filepath.Join(dir, "todo-server")
	// #nosec G204 -- the command is a literal; only the output path, chosen
	// right here, varies.
	cmd := exec.Command("go", "build", "-o", binPath, ".")
	cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("build test binary: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}

// syncBuffer is a bytes.Buffer whose writes and reads are guarded. exec's
// copying goroutines write while the test polls the process, and the race
// detector would flag an unguarded read; a plain buffer would race.
type syncBuffer struct {
	mu  sync.Mutex
	buf bytes.Buffer
}

// Write appends p, safely.
func (b *syncBuffer) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	return b.buf.Write(p)
}

// String returns everything written so far, safely.
func (b *syncBuffer) String() string {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	return b.buf.String()
}

// serverProcess is one started server binary: the command, its address, the
// directory its files live in, its captured output, and the channel Wait's
// error arrives on.
type serverProcess struct {
	cmd    *exec.Cmd
	addr   string
	dir    string
	stdout *syncBuffer
	stderr *syncBuffer
	wait   chan error
}

// startServer starts the binary on a free port with a deliberately bare
// environment and polls liveness, so every case begins with a server that
// answers. The environment is PATH so the process starts, and the two
// variables that pin the app's paths. HOME and the XDG variables are absent
// on purpose; with TODO_DB and TODO_LOG set, and the listen address passed as
// a flag, the binary must not need either. extraEnv appends the variables a
// case is about — the admin key and the account it names — after the bare
// ones, so a case cannot lose the paths it needs.
func startServer(t *testing.T, extraEnv ...string) *serverProcess {
	t.Helper()
	dir := t.TempDir()

	// A free port: bind one, read it, release it. The release and the
	// server's bind race the rest of the machine — the kernel may hand the
	// port to someone else first — but the failure mode is loud: the server
	// exits with a bind error, and the poll below reports it.
	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	addr := ln.Addr().String()
	require.NoError(t, ln.Close())

	// #nosec G204 -- binPath is built by TestMain from this package's own
	// source, and the arguments are test-authored.
	cmd := exec.Command(binPath, "--listen", addr)
	cmd.Env = append([]string{
		"PATH=" + os.Getenv("PATH"),
		"TODO_DB=" + filepath.Join(dir, "todo.db"),
		"TODO_LOG=" + filepath.Join(dir, "todo.log"),
	}, extraEnv...)
	stdout, stderr := &syncBuffer{}, &syncBuffer{}
	cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = stdout, stderr
	require.NoError(t, cmd.Start())

	// Wait runs in the background from here on: the poll below must notice a
	// server that died at startup instead of waiting out the deadline on a
	// corpse. Receiving from waitErr also means the process was reaped and
	// the output buffers are final, so reading them is safe.
	waitErr := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() { waitErr <- cmd.Wait() }()

	// Poll liveness until the server answers. The first answer is normally
	// immediate; the loop exists so a slow start is a wait, not a flake.
	healthz := "http://" + addr + "/healthz"
	deadline := time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second)
	for {
		resp, err := http.Get(healthz) // #nosec G107 -- the URL is the test's own listener address
		if err == nil {
			require.NoError(t, resp.Body.Close())
			require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, resp.StatusCode)
			break
		}
		select {
		case werr := <-waitErr:
			require.Failf(t, "server exited before answering /healthz", "wait: %v; stderr:\n%s", werr, stderr.String())
		case <-time.After(25 * time.Millisecond):
		}
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			_ = cmd.Process.Kill()
			<-waitErr
			require.Failf(t, "no answer on /healthz", "stderr:\n%s", stderr.String())
		}
	}

	return &serverProcess{cmd: cmd, addr: addr, dir: dir, stdout: stdout, stderr: stderr, wait: waitErr}
}

// stop sends SIGTERM, the signal a service manager sends, and requires the
// process to drain and exit 0, not die by signal.
func (s *serverProcess) stop(t *testing.T) {
	t.Helper()
	require.NoError(t, s.cmd.Process.Signal(syscall.SIGTERM))
	select {
	case err := <-s.wait:
		require.NoError(t, err, "the server must exit 0 on SIGTERM; stderr:\n%s", s.stderr.String())
	case <-time.After(10 * time.Second):
		_ = s.cmd.Process.Kill()
		<-s.wait
		t.Fatal("the server did not exit after SIGTERM")
	}
}

// postJSON posts a JSON body to url and returns the response. Nothing here
// imports internal/api — the subject is the binary, exactly as a service
// manager sees it.
func postJSON(t *testing.T, url, body string, mutate func(*http.Request)) *http.Response {
	t.Helper()
	req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, url, strings.NewReader(body))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	if mutate != nil {
		mutate(req)
	}
	resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	return resp
}

// postForm posts an urlencoded form — the shape every page submits — and
// returns the response. The client does not follow redirects: a form's
// answer is the redirect itself, and following it would turn every status
// assertion into the target page's.
func postForm(t *testing.T, url string, values url.Values, cookies ...*http.Cookie) *http.Response {
	t.Helper()
	req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, url, strings.NewReader(values.Encode()))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
	for _, cookie := range cookies {
		req.AddCookie(cookie)
	}
	resp, err := noRedirect.Do(req) // #nosec G107 -- the test's own listener address
	require.NoError(t, err)
	return resp
}

// fetchPage GETs url with the cookies presented and returns the response and
// its body. The cookie travels back by hand for the same reason as in the
// auth flow: it is marked Secure, and this is a plain-http socket. Like
// postForm, the client does not follow redirects.
func fetchPage(t *testing.T, url string, cookies ...*http.Cookie) (*http.Response, string) {
	t.Helper()
	req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, url, nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	for _, cookie := range cookies {
		req.AddCookie(cookie)
	}
	resp, err := noRedirect.Do(req) // #nosec G107 -- the test's own listener address
	require.NoError(t, err)
	body, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, resp.Body.Close())
	return resp, string(body)
}

// noRedirect is the client the page flow drives: every page assertion is
// about the redirect itself — its 303 and its Location — so the client must
// not follow it. http.DefaultClient would follow a 303 to the target page
// and hand back its 200, which is what the first run of the process-level
// flow discovered.
var noRedirect = &http.Client{
	CheckRedirect: func(*http.Request, []*http.Request) error { return http.ErrUseLastResponse },
}

// The regexps the flow reads out of a page: the token every form embeds,
// the first task row's edit link and version — the values a browser carries
// back in the row's forms — and the stylesheet's URL. templ renders
// attributes in source order.
var (
	csrfField      = regexp.MustCompile(`name="csrf_token" value="([^"]+)"`)
	editLink       = regexp.MustCompile(`href="/tasks/([0-9a-f-]+)/edit"`)
	versionField   = regexp.MustCompile(`name="version" value="(\d+)"`)
	stylesheetLink = regexp.MustCompile(`<link rel="stylesheet" href="([^"]+)">`)
)

// csrfFrom extracts the first CSRF token a page carries.
func csrfFrom(t *testing.T, body string) string {
	t.Helper()
	m := csrfField.FindStringSubmatch(body)
	require.Len(t, m, 2, "the page carries a CSRF token field")
	return m[1]
}

// firstTask extracts the id and version of the page's first task row.
func firstTask(t *testing.T, body string) (id, version string) {
	t.Helper()
	edit := editLink.FindStringSubmatch(body)
	require.Len(t, edit, 2, "the page lists a task")
	ver := versionField.FindStringSubmatch(body)
	require.Len(t, ver, 2, "the row carries the version")
	return edit[1], ver[1]
}

// sessionCookie returns the session cookie a response set, or nil when it
// set none. A cleared cookie — an empty value — names no session. The name
// is the production one, __Host- prefix included: the black-box test reads
// the cookie the way a browser would, and the prefix is part of its
// identity.
func sessionCookie(resp *http.Response) *http.Cookie {
	for _, cookie := range resp.Cookies() {
		if cookie.Name == "__Host-session" && cookie.Value != "" {
			return cookie
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// TestServer_Lifecycle is the process-level contract: the server starts,
// answers liveness, and exits 0 on SIGTERM, with structured records of the
// lifecycle on stderr and in the log file.
func TestServer_Lifecycle(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	srv := startServer(t)
	srv.stop(t)

	// The structured record is the server's announcement: stdout stays empty
	// — chapter 29's channel rule; a server serves data over HTTP — and both
	// lifecycle events land on stderr as JSON.
	assert.Empty(t, srv.stdout.String(), "a server's stdout is data, and it serves data over HTTP")
	assert.Contains(t, srv.stderr.String(), `"msg":"server listening"`)
	assert.Contains(t, srv.stderr.String(), `"msg":"shutting down"`)
	assert.Contains(t, srv.stderr.String(), `"msg":"server stopped"`)

	// The log file is the durable half of the tee: the same records, on disk.
	logData, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(srv.dir, "todo.log")) // #nosec G304 -- the test's own temp path
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Contains(t, string(logData), `"msg":"server listening"`)
	assert.Contains(t, string(logData), `"msg":"server stopped"`)
}

// TestServer_IndexPage drives the web surface through the real binary: the
// page is mounted by main on the same instance the API serves, it sits
// behind the same gate, and it renders the logged-in user's tasks from the
// same store the API writes. The anonymous half is the only place a missing
// mount would show — the binary would answer 404 where the gate's redirect
// belongs — which is why this case exists at the process level: the mount is
// main's line, and nothing below main can test it. The redirect is chapter
// 37's seam: chapter 36's notes left the anonymous answer at the API's 401
// and said the login form would move it, and this is where it moved.
func TestServer_IndexPage(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	srv := startServer(t)
	defer srv.stop(t)

	base := "http://" + srv.addr

	resp, _ := fetchPage(t, base+"/")
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusSeeOther, resp.StatusCode)
	require.Equal(t, "/login", resp.Header.Get("Location"))

	// A real session through the real login route, and a task through the
	// real API: the page reads what the API wrote.
	resp = postJSON(t, base+"/api/v1/auth/register", `{"email":"ada@example.com","password":"correct horse battery staple"}`, nil)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, resp.StatusCode)
	require.NoError(t, resp.Body.Close())

	resp = postJSON(t, base+"/api/v1/auth/login", `{"email":"ada@example.com","password":"correct horse battery staple"}`, nil)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, resp.StatusCode)
	cookies := resp.Cookies()
	require.NoError(t, resp.Body.Close())
	require.Len(t, cookies, 1, "login sets the session cookie")

	resp = postJSON(t, base+"/api/v1/tasks", `{"title":"buy milk"}`, func(req *http.Request) {
		req.AddCookie(cookies[0])
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, resp.StatusCode)
	require.NoError(t, resp.Body.Close())

	// The cookie travels back by hand for the same reason as in the auth
	// flow: it is marked Secure, and this is a plain-http socket.
	resp, body := fetchPage(t, base+"/", cookies[0])
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, resp.StatusCode)
	assert.Contains(t, resp.Header.Get("Content-Type"), "text/html")
	assert.Contains(t, body, "<title>Tasks</title>")
	assert.Contains(t, body, "buy milk")
}

// TestServer_AuthFlow drives register, login, and logout through the real
// binary over a real socket: the chapter's whole wiring — the schema, the
// password hash, the session store, and the cookie — end to end, the way the
// TUI and the web pages will use it.
func TestServer_AuthFlow(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	srv := startServer(t)
	defer srv.stop(t)

	base := "http://" + srv.addr + "/api/v1/auth"

	resp := postJSON(t, base+"/register", `{"email":"alice@example.com","password":"correct horse battery staple"}`, nil)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, resp.StatusCode)
	require.NoError(t, resp.Body.Close())

	resp = postJSON(t, base+"/login", `{"email":"alice@example.com","password":"correct horse battery staple"}`, nil)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, resp.StatusCode)
	cookies := resp.Cookies()
	require.NoError(t, resp.Body.Close())
	require.Len(t, cookies, 1, "login sets the session cookie")
	require.True(t, cookies[0].Secure)
	require.True(t, cookies[0].HttpOnly)

	// The cookie travels back by hand: it is marked Secure, and this is a
	// plain-http socket, so no cookie jar would send it — browsers and jars
	// enforce the flag, the server cannot.
	resp = postJSON(t, base+"/logout", "", func(req *http.Request) {
		req.AddCookie(cookies[0])
	})
	require.NoError(t, resp.Body.Close())
	assert.Equal(t, http.StatusNoContent, resp.StatusCode)
}

// TestServer_WebForms drives the chapter's whole browser-shaped flow through
// the real binary over a real socket: the anonymous redirect, the login form
// and its post, create → redirect → GET with the flash, edit, complete,
// delete, and logout — every post carrying the token the page embedded, and
// every write landing in the same store the JSON edge reads.
func TestServer_WebForms(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	srv := startServer(t)
	defer srv.stop(t)

	base := "http://" + srv.addr

	// The API registers the account; the forms log it in.
	resp := postJSON(t, base+"/api/v1/auth/register", `{"email":"ada@example.com","password":"correct horse battery staple"}`, nil)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, resp.StatusCode)
	require.NoError(t, resp.Body.Close())

	// An anonymous task page is a 303 to the login form.
	resp, _ = fetchPage(t, base+"/")
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusSeeOther, resp.StatusCode)
	require.Equal(t, "/login", resp.Header.Get("Location"))

	// The login page starts the session its token lives in.
	resp, body := fetchPage(t, base+"/login")
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, resp.StatusCode)
	cookie := sessionCookie(resp)
	require.NotNil(t, cookie, "the login page sets the session cookie")

	resp = postForm(t, base+"/login", url.Values{
		"csrf_token": {csrfFrom(t, body)},
		"email":      {"ada@example.com"},
		"password":   {"correct horse battery staple"},
	}, cookie)
	require.NoError(t, resp.Body.Close())
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusSeeOther, resp.StatusCode)
	if fresh := sessionCookie(resp); fresh != nil {
		cookie = fresh
	}

	// The redirect's target is the list, and the flash says who logged in.
	resp, body = fetchPage(t, base+"/", cookie)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, resp.StatusCode)
	require.Contains(t, body, "Logged in as ada@example.com.")

	// Create: the post is a 303, and the list shows the task and the flash.
	resp = postForm(t, base+"/tasks", url.Values{
		"csrf_token": {csrfFrom(t, body)},
		"title":      {"buy milk"},
	}, cookie)
	require.NoError(t, resp.Body.Close())
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusSeeOther, resp.StatusCode)
	require.Equal(t, "/", resp.Header.Get("Location"))

	resp, body = fetchPage(t, base+"/", cookie)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, resp.StatusCode)
	require.Contains(t, body, "Task created.")
	require.Contains(t, body, "buy milk")
	id, version := firstTask(t, body)

	// The JSON edge reads the same store the form wrote.
	resp, apiBody := fetchPage(t, base+"/api/v1/tasks", cookie)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, resp.StatusCode)
	require.Contains(t, apiBody, "buy milk", "the forms and the API ride one store")

	// Edit: the form re-renders the stored values, and the post saves them.
	resp, body = fetchPage(t, base+"/tasks/"+id+"/edit", cookie)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, resp.StatusCode)
	require.Contains(t, body, `value="buy milk"`)

	resp = postForm(t, base+"/tasks/"+id, url.Values{
		"csrf_token": {csrfFrom(t, body)},
		"version":    {version},
		"title":      {"buy oat milk"},
		"priority":   {"5"},
		"due":        {"2026-11-01"},
		"tags":       {"errands, home"},
	}, cookie)
	require.NoError(t, resp.Body.Close())
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusSeeOther, resp.StatusCode)

	resp, body = fetchPage(t, base+"/", cookie)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, resp.StatusCode)
	require.Contains(t, body, "Task saved.")
	require.Contains(t, body, "buy oat milk")
	require.Contains(t, body, "due 2026-11-01")
	require.Contains(t, body, "errands, home")
	id, version = firstTask(t, body)

	// Complete: the row's button is a post, and the redirect shows Done.
	resp = postForm(t, base+"/tasks/"+id+"/complete", url.Values{
		"csrf_token": {csrfFrom(t, body)},
		"version":    {version},
	}, cookie)
	require.NoError(t, resp.Body.Close())
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusSeeOther, resp.StatusCode)

	resp, body = fetchPage(t, base+"/", cookie)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, resp.StatusCode)
	require.Contains(t, body, "Task completed.")
	require.Contains(t, body, `<span class="status">Done</span>`)
	_, version = firstTask(t, body)

	// Delete: the task goes from the page and from the API.
	resp = postForm(t, base+"/tasks/"+id+"/delete", url.Values{
		"csrf_token": {csrfFrom(t, body)},
		"version":    {version},
	}, cookie)
	require.NoError(t, resp.Body.Close())
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusSeeOther, resp.StatusCode)

	resp, body = fetchPage(t, base+"/", cookie)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, resp.StatusCode)
	require.Contains(t, body, "Task deleted.")
	require.NotContains(t, body, "buy oat milk")

	resp, apiBody = fetchPage(t, base+"/api/v1/tasks", cookie)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, resp.StatusCode)
	require.NotContains(t, apiBody, "buy oat milk")

	// Logout: the post destroys the session, the login page says so, and
	// the task pages are anonymous again.
	resp = postForm(t, base+"/logout", url.Values{"csrf_token": {csrfFrom(t, body)}}, cookie)
	require.NoError(t, resp.Body.Close())
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusSeeOther, resp.StatusCode)
	require.Equal(t, "/login", resp.Header.Get("Location"))
	if fresh := sessionCookie(resp); fresh != nil {
		cookie = fresh
	}

	resp, body = fetchPage(t, base+"/login", cookie)
````
